{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1794645954123,"sessionID":"ses_e26c3f8acffeWBLPvCcDgQ9v3e","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"read","callID":"toolu_019EvDvZbVY1YuF6tgBeaEf3","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/app/SPEC_WATCH.md"},"output":"<path>/app/SPEC_WATCH.md</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: # Watch gear train: specification\n2: \n3: ## The job\n4: \n5: Design the gear train of a mechanical wristwatch, as 3D-printable parts. The work\n6: is done in four stages, each by a different engineer who starts from the result\n7: of the stage before:\n8: \n9: 1. **Design** the movement (this document up to \"Stage 2\").\n10: 2. **Extend** it with a 24-hour hand, without touching the existing wheels.\n11: 3. **Change** it: the barrel now turns faster; rework the movement for that while\n12:    keeping as many of the received part files as you can.\n13: 4. **Assemble** it: an order and a collision-free path for every part.\n14: \n15: Your instruction file says which stage you are doing. Read the later stages too:\n16: what you design in stage 1 has to survive them, and the size limit is the same\n17: at every stage.\n18: \n19: The mainspring barrel is supplied (`meshes/barrel.stl`). It turns **clockwise,\n20: once every 8 hours** (at stage 3 it turns once every 6 hours; see \"Stage 3\").\n21: Drive the watch's **hour, minute and seconds hands** from it. There is no\n22: escapement and no winding or setting mechanism in this task: the barrel is simply\n23: the driver, and the grader turns it at that steady speed.\n24: \n25: You make every other part: wheels, pinions, arbors, plates, bridges and the three\n26: hands.\n27: \n28: ## Frame and units\n29: \n30: Millimetres. Right-handed frame. **Every arbor (rotation axis) is parallel to z.**\n31: The dial side is +z: the hands are read looking from +z towards -z, and\n32: \"clockwise\" always means clockwise in that view.\n33: \n34: ## The supplied barrel\n35: \n36: `meshes/barrel.stl`, fixed where it is: axis on x = 0, y = 0.\n37: \n38: - A spur gear of 96 teeth, module 0.2 (pitch diameter 19.2), z 0 to 1.0.\n39:   Involute teeth, pressure angle 25 degrees, addendum 1.0 x module, dedendum\n40:   1.25 x module, tooth thickness on the pitch circle reduced by 0.03 for\n41:   backlash. One tooth is centred on the +x direction.\n42: - An arbor of radius 0.5 from z -1.0 to z 1.6.\n43: \n44: The barrel is a mobile named `barrel`. You must hold it like any other mobile.\n45: The name `barrel` is reserved: none of your parts or mobiles may be called\n46: `barrel` (a file that does so fails the Files requirement).\n47: \n48: ## What you submit\n49: \n50: A folder `work/` containing `movement.json` and one STEP file per part,\n51: `parts/<name>.step`, made with a CAD kernel (CadQuery 2.8.0 / OpenCASCADE is\n52: installed). STL part files are not accepted. Keep the scripts that made your\n53: parts in `scripts/`; they are copied with your submission and archived with it,\n54: but nothing in them is run or graded. **A later stage does not receive your\n55: scripts**: the next engineer gets only `movement.json` and the `parts/` STEP\n56: files (in `work/` and again in `previous/`), and reworks the movement from\n57: those files alone.\n58: \n59: The supplied barrel is the one exception: it is given as a mesh,\n60: `meshes/barrel.stl` (binary STL, millimetres, in its place). You do not submit\n61: it. To use it in your own checks, load it as a `manifold3d` solid, for example\n62: with `tools/kernel.py`: `kernel.tris_to_manifold(kernel.read_stl(path, 200000,\n63: 33554432))`.\n64: \n65: Each part is in its assembled position. At most 60 parts. Part and mobile\n66: names use letters, digits, `_` and `-`, 1 to 40 characters; `barrel` is taken\n67: by the supplied barrel and may not name a part or another mobile. Tooth counts\n68: in `meshes` are integers from 3 to 1000. `movement.json` may be at most\n69: 1,048,576 bytes and `assembly.json` at most 67,108,864 bytes. Every file the\n70: grader opens (`movement.json`, `assembly.json`, each part file, and the `parts/`\n71: folder) must be a real file or folder inside the submission folder: a symbolic\n72: link, or a file outside the folder, is a format error. How a part file becomes the solid that every test\n73: below uses:\n74: \n75: - At most 16,777,216 bytes. The file's length unit must be millimetre; a file\n76:   in any other unit (inch, metre, ...) is rejected, not converted. It must hold\n77:   exactly one solid, valid by OpenCASCADE's shape check, and nothing outside\n78:   that solid. A file whose solid has more than 500 flat faces with exactly three\n79:   edges is rejected (the rule counts only such triangular faces). Reading and meshing one file may take\n80:   at most 120 s and 4,096 MB of memory (it runs in its own process).\n81: - The solid is meshed with OpenCASCADE (`BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh`) with a\n82:   linear deflection of 0.001 mm (absolute) and an angular deflection of 0.1\n83:   radians. A meshed curved surface lies within 0.001 mm of the true one (inside\n84:   a convex surface, outside a concave one, such as a hole).\n85: - The mesh may have at most 200,000 triangles; the triangles, with identical\n86:   vertices joined, must form a single closed manifold shell with positive\n87:   volume, and its volume may change by at most 0.5% when the solid is united\n88:   with itself.\n89: \n90: `movement.json`:\n91: \n92: ```\n93: {\n94:   \"case_centre\": [x, y],\n95:   \"fixed\": [\"main_plate\", \"bridge\", ...],\n96:   \"mobiles\": {\n97:     \"some_name\": {\"axis\": [x, y], \"parts\": [\"wheel_a\", \"arbor_a\", ...]},\n98:     ...\n99:   },\n100:   \"meshes\": [\n101:     {\"driver\": \"barrel\", \"driver_teeth\": 96, \"driven\": \"some_name\", \"driven_teeth\": 12},\n102:     ...\n103:   ],\n104:   \"hands\": {\n105:     \"hour\":    {\"mobile\": \"...\", \"part\": \"...\"},\n106:     \"minute\":  {\"mobile\": \"...\", \"part\": \"...\"},\n107:     \"seconds\": {\"mobile\": \"...\", \"part\": \"...\"}\n108:   }\n109: }\n110: ```\n111: \n112: - `fixed`: parts that do not move (plates, bridges, pillars, cocks). Fixed parts\n113:   must not overlap one another.\n114: - `mobiles`: each mobile is a set of parts that turn together as one rigid body\n115:   about the vertical line through `axis`. Parts of one mobile may overlap each\n116:   other. Do not list `barrel`; it already exists.\n117: - `meshes`: every pair of gears that drive one another, with the tooth count of\n118:   the gear on each mobile. All meshes are external (the two mobiles turn in\n119:   opposite directions). Speeds are worked out from these tooth counts as exact\n120:   fractions, starting from the barrel.\n121: - `hands`: which mobile carries each hand, and which of that mobile's parts is\n122:   the hand.\n123: - A part may be used only once.\n124: \n125: ## Hard requirements\n126: \n127: If either fails the score is 0.\n128: \n129: - Files: `movement.json` and every part it names are valid as described above.\n130: - Assembled: in the positions given, the fixed parts taken together and each\n131:   mobile (the barrel included) intersect one another by at most 0.01 mm3, and no\n132:   two fixed parts intersect each other by more than 0.01 mm3.\n133: \n134: ## Scored requirements\n135: \n136: Each passes or fails. Weights in brackets; the total is 17.\n137: \n138: - **Free to turn [1].** Each mobile, turned through a full turn in 72 steps of 5\n139:   degrees, never intersects the fixed parts by more than 0.01 mm3.\n140: - **Held [2].** Each mobile, the barrel included, is moved 0.3 along +x, -x, +y,\n141:   -y, +z and -z in turn and must intersect what holds it by more than 0.01 mm3\n142:   every time. For the four sideways moves, anything else counts (fixed parts and\n143:   other mobiles). For the two moves along z, only the fixed parts and mobiles on\n144:   the same axis (within 0.01) count: a wheel may not be kept in place by a wheel\n145:   on a different arbor. So each mobile can turn but cannot wander.\n146: - **The train runs [3].** No mobile is given two different speeds by the\n147:   declared meshes, each of the three hand mobiles is driven from the barrel, and\n148:   every declared mesh passes this test. Starting from the assembled position,\n149:   at step i (i = 0, 1, ..., 8 x max(driver teeth, driven teeth) - 1) the driver\n150:   is turned counter-clockwise (seen from +z) by i x 360 / (8 x driver teeth)\n151:   degrees about its axis and the driven mobile clockwise by that angle x driver\n152:   teeth / driven teeth about its own. Then\n153:   - at every step the two mobiles intersect by at most 0.01 mm3 (no jam);\n154:   - at every fourth step the smallest distance between them is at most 0.1\n155:     (they stay engaged);\n156:   - at every eighth step, turning the driver a further quarter of its tooth\n157:     pitch (90 / driver teeth degrees, counter-clockwise) while the driven mobile\n158:     is held makes them intersect by more than 0.01 mm3 (the teeth really drive).\n159: - **Nothing else collides [1].** Every pair of mobiles that does not mesh is\n160:   turned together at the speeds the tooth counts give (a mobile that is not\n161:   driven stands still): 144 equal steps covering one full turn of the faster of\n162:   the two, then 144 equal steps covering one full turn of one relative to the\n163:   other. At every step they intersect by at most 0.01 mm3.\n164: - **Hour hand [2], minute hand [2], seconds hand [2], hand arrangement [1].** The\n165:   watch must tell the time: the hands must move as the hands of a watch do. A\n166:   hand is driven only through meshes that pass the test of \"The train runs\": a\n167:   declared mesh that fails that test drives nothing, so the hand speeds are\n168:   worked out from the barrel through the passing meshes only. (The same holds\n169:   for the 24-hour hand of stages 2 and 3.)\n170: - **Hands reach [1].** Each hand part reaches at least 5.0 from its axis.\n171: - **Size [1].** Everything, as it turns, stays within 20.7 of the vertical line\n172:   through `case_centre`, and the whole movement including the barrel is at most\n173:   13.4 tall in z. These limits are the same at every stage.\n174: - **Printable [1].** The smallest printable feature is 0.2. Each of your parts\n175:   (not the barrel) is tested like this: it is turned into voxels on a 0.05 grid,\n176:   a voxel being solid when its centre is inside the part. A solid voxel survives\n177:   if its centre is at least 0.075 (1.5 voxels) from the centre of the nearest\n178:   voxel that is not solid. The printable body is every solid voxel whose centre\n179:   is within 0.05 of a surviving voxel's centre. The part passes if something\n180:   survives and no solid voxel's centre is further than 0.2 from the printable\n181:   body. Ordinary gear teeth of module 0.12 or more pass; a wall, web or roof 0.2\n182:   thick or less does not. How the grid lines up with your part is not fixed, so\n183:   leave a little margin.\n184: \n185: ## Score\n186: \n187: ```\n188: p     = (weight of scored requirements passed) / 17\n189: score = 0 if a hard requirement fails, otherwise\n190: score = 0.5 * p^2 + 0.5 * (1 if every scored requirement passes, else 0)\n191: ```\n192: \n193: ## Stage 2: add a 24-hour hand\n194: \n195: You receive a finished stage-1 movement in `work/` (the same files are in\n196: `previous/` for reference). Add a **24-hour hand**: a fourth hand that shows day\n197: and night. Declare it as `\"day\"` under `hands`.\n198: \n199: What is frozen:\n200: \n201: - every mobile of the received movement keeps its name and its axis (the same\n202:   two numbers, unchanged);\n203: - every part file of those mobiles stays byte-for-byte the same and stays in its\n204:   mobile (you may add new parts to a mobile);\n205: - every declared mesh stays, and the hour, minute and seconds entries under\n206:   `hands` stay.\n207: \n208: You may add mobiles, add parts, add meshes, and replace or add fixed parts.\n209: \n210: Hard requirements: the two of stage 1, the frozen items above, and a 24-hour\n211: hand is declared (`hands.day` names a mobile and one of that mobile's parts,\n212: and that part is a new part, not one of the received parts).\n213: \n214: Scored requirements (total weight 21): all eleven of stage 1, still passing with\n215: their weights, plus\n216: \n217: - **24-hour hand [3].** It moves as a 24-hour hand does.\n218: - **24-hour hand placement [1].** Its axis is at least 6.0 from the hour hand's\n219:   axis, and the hand part reaches at least 3.0 from its own axis.\n220: \n221: Score: the stage-1 formula with p out of 21.\n222: \n223: ## Stage 3: change request, a faster barrel\n224: \n225: You receive a finished stage-2 movement in `work/` (the same files are in\n226: `previous/` for reference). The barrel is replaced by one that is identical in\n227: every way (same `meshes/barrel.stl`, same place, same teeth) except that it turns\n228: **clockwise once every 6 hours** instead of once every 8. Rework the movement so\n229: that it meets every requirement of stage 2 with this barrel, and keep as many of\n230: the received part files as you can.\n231: \n232: Nothing is frozen: you may change, add, remove and rename anything. The hard\n233: requirements are the two of stage 1, plus: **the change request is met**, that\n234: is, the hour hand, minute hand, seconds hand and 24-hour hand requirements all\n235: pass with the barrel turning once every 6 hours. The scored requirements are all thirteen of\n236: stage 2 with their weights (total 21), tested with the barrel turning once every\n237: 6 hours. The hands must still move as the hands of a watch do, and the 24-hour\n238: hand as a 24-hour hand does.\n239: \n240: Kept parts. A received part (a part named in the received `movement.json`) is\n241: **kept** if its file in your submission is byte-for-byte the same as the received\n242: file and\n243: \n244: - for a received fixed part: it is still listed under `fixed`;\n245: - for a received part of a mobile: it is still in a mobile of the same name, whose\n246:   axis is the same as the received mobile's axis (the same two numbers,\n247:   unchanged), and that mobile is driven from the barrel through declared meshes\n248:   that pass the test of \"The train runs\".\n249: \n250: A received file that is not named in your `movement.json`, that moves to another\n251: mobile, to a renamed mobile or to `fixed`, or that sits on a mobile nothing drives,\n252: is not kept.\n253: \n254: ```\n255: kept share = (received part files that are kept) / (received part files)\n256: factor     = min(1, kept share / (15/17))\n257: p          = (weight of scored requirements passed) / 21\n258: score      = 0 if a hard requirement fails, otherwise\n259: score      = (0.5 * p^2 + 0.5 * (1 if every scored requirement passes, else 0)) * factor\n260: ```\n261: \n262: The share counts part files: each file counts once, whatever its size or what it\n263: holds. 15/17 (about 0.882) is the kept share of a reference solution, which keeps 15 of\n264: the 17 part files it receives. The factor is exactly 1 at a kept share of 15/17\n265: or more.\n266: \n267: ## Stage 4: assemble it\n268: \n269: You receive a finished stage-3 movement in `work/` (also in `previous/`).\n270: `movement.json` and every part file are frozen: byte-for-byte unchanged.\n271: \n272: Write `work/assembly.json`:\n273: \n274: ```\n275: {\"order\": [\"part_name\", ...], \"paths\": {\"part_name\": [P, P, ...], ...}}\n276: ```\n277: \n278: `order` lists every part named in `movement.json`, and `barrel`, in the order\n279: they are put in. A name that is not a part is ignored; a name that appears more\n280: than once counts at its first place only. A part that is not in `order` is not\n281: installed, and it stands in its assembled position from the start, so every part\n282: in `order` is tested against it. Each P is a 4x4 matrix as four rows of four numbers that moves\n283: the part from its assembled position (`world = R * assembled + t`, last row\n284: `0 0 0 1`); the parts are given in their assembled position, so the last pose of\n285: every path is the identity.\n286: \n287: Rules for a path:\n288: \n289: 1. Every matrix is finite and a proper rotation plus translation (R^T R = I and\n290:    det R = +1, within 1e-6); the last pose is the identity within 1e-6.\n291: 2. In the first pose the part's bounding box lies wholly outside the bounding box\n292:    of the complete movement (all parts and the barrel, assembled) grown by 5.0 on\n293:    every side.\n294: 3. Between consecutive poses no vertex of the part moves more than 0.2.\n295: 4. At least 2 and at most 1,500 poses.\n296: 5. In every pose the part intersects each part placed before it by at most\n297:    0.01 mm3. Parts of the same mobile are pressed onto each other and are not\n298:    tested against one another. The barrel counts as a part of the mobile `barrel`.\n299: \n300: A part whose path obeys rules 1 to 5 is installed. A part that breaks a rule is\n301: not installed, but it still stands in its assembled position for the parts that\n302: follow.\n303: \n304: ```\n305: p     = (parts installed) / (all parts, the barrel included)\n306: score = 0 if the Files requirement of stage 1 fails, if movement.json or a part file was changed,\n307:         or if assembly.json cannot be read\n308: score = 0.5 * p^2 + 0.5 * (1 if every part is installed, else 0)\n309: ```\n310: \n311: ## What you are given to work with\n312: \n313: There are no measuring tools and no copy of the grader's test code. Every test\n314: above is defined completely by its numbers, so you can build your own checks.\n315: \n316: - Python 3 with `cadquery` 2.8.0 (OpenCASCADE, importable as `cadquery` and\n317:   `OCP`), `manifold3d`, `trimesh`, `numpy` and `scipy`.\n318: - `tools/kernel.py`: small helpers on top of `manifold3d` (read and write STL,\n319:   used for the supplied barrel and for your own checks; rigid transform, intersection volume, smallest distance, cross-section), plus\n320:   `write_step(path, shape)` (a CadQuery object or OCP shape, written in\n321:   millimetres) and `load_step_part(...)`, which turns a STEP file into the same\n322:   `manifold3d` solid the grader uses. `python3 tools/submit.py` calls it with the\n323:   numbers stated under \"What you submit\", so a part that submit accepts is the\n324:   solid the tests see.\n325: - `meshes/barrel.stl` (the supplied barrel, the only mesh; your parts are STEP).\n326: - `python3 tools/submit.py`: checks the file format only (JSON structure, part\n327:   names, each part file read and turned into a solid exactly as described under\n328:   \"What you submit\") and copies your work to the submission folder: the\n329:   `movement.json`, the part files it names, `assembly.json` if present, and\n330:   `scripts/` (at most 200 files and 4,194,304 bytes; larger is a format error).\n331:   It answers \"accepted\" or a format error. It runs none of the tests.\n332: \n333: Only the submission folder as it is when you stop is graded. You may submit as\n334: often as you like; the last accepted submission counts.\n\n(End of file - total 334 lines)\n</content>","metadata":{"preview":"# Watch gear train: specification\n\n## The job\n\nDesign the gear train of a mechanical wristwatch, as 3D-printable parts. Read the later stages too:\nwhat you design in stage 1 has to survive them, and the size limit is the same\nat every stage.\n\nThe mainspring barrel is supplied (`meshes/barrel.stl`). It turns **clockwise,\nonce every 8 hours** (at stage 3 it turns once every 6 hours; see \"Stage 3\").\nDrive the watch's **hour, minute and seconds hands** from it. There is no\nescapement and no winding or setting mechanism in this task: the barrel is simply\nthe driver, and the grader turns it at that steady speed.\n\nYou make every other part: wheels, pinions, arbors, plates, bridges and the three\nhands.\n\n## Frame and units\n\nMillimetres. Right-handed frame. **Every arbor (rotation axis) is parallel to z.**\nThe dial side is +z: the hands are read looking from +z towards -z, and\n\"clockwise\" always means clockwise in that view.\n\n## The supplied barrel\n\n`meshes/barrel.stl`, fixed where it is: axis on x = 0, y = 0.\n\n- A spur gear of 96 teeth, module 0.2 (pitch diameter 19.2), z 0 to 1.0.\n  Involute teeth, pressure angle 25 degrees, addendum 1.0 x module, dedendum\n  1.25 x module, tooth thickness on the pitch circle reduced by 0.03 for\n  backlash. One tooth is centred on the +x direction.\n- An arbor of radius 0.5 from z -1.0 to z 1.6.\n\nThe barrel is a mobile named `barrel`. You must hold it like any other mobile.\nThe name `barrel` is reserved: none of your parts or mobiles may be called\n`barrel` (a file that does so fails the Files requirement).\n\n## What you submit\n\nA folder `work/` containing `movement.json` and one STEP file per part,\n`parts/<name>.step`, made with a CAD kernel (CadQuery 2.8.0 / OpenCASCADE is\ninstalled). STL part files are not accepted. Keep the scripts that made your\nparts in `scripts/`; they are copied with your submission and archived with it,\nbut nothing in them is run or graded. **A later stage does not receive your\nscripts**: the next engineer gets only `movement.json` and the `parts/` STEP\nfiles (in `work/` and again in `previous/`), and reworks the movement from\nthose files alone.\n\nThe supplied barrel is the one exception: it is given as a mesh,\n`meshes/barrel.stl` (binary STL, millimetres, in its place). You do not submit\nit. To use it in your own checks, load it as a `manifold3d` solid, for example\nwith `tools/kernel.py`: `kernel.tris_to_manifold(kernel.read_stl(path, 200000,\n33554432))`.\n\nEach part is in its assembled position. At most 60 parts. Part and mobile\nnames use letters, digits, `_` and `-`, 1 to 40 characters; `barrel` is taken\nby the supplied barrel and may not name a part or another mobile. Tooth counts\nin `meshes` are integers from 3 to 1000. `movement.json` may be at most\n1,048,576 bytes and `assembly.json` at most 67,108,864 bytes. Every file the\ngrader opens (`movement.json`, `assembly.json`, each part file, and the `parts/`\nfolder) must be a real file or folder inside the submission folder: a symbolic\nlink, or a file outside the folder, is a format error. How a part file becomes the solid that every test\nbelow uses:\n\n- At most 16,777,216 bytes. The file's length unit must be millimetre; a file\n  in any other unit (inch, metre, ...) is rejected, not converted. It must hold\n  exactly one solid, valid by OpenCASCADE's shape check, and nothing outside\n  that solid. A file whose solid has more than 500 flat faces with exactly three\n  edges is rejected (the rule counts only such triangular faces). Reading and meshing one file may take\n  at most 120 s and 4,096 MB of memory (it runs in its own process).\n- The solid is meshed with OpenCASCADE (`BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh`) with a\n  linear deflection of 0.001 mm (absolute) and an angular deflection of 0.1\n  radians. A meshed curved surface lies within 0.001 mm of the true one (inside\n  a convex surface, outside a concave one, such as a hole).\n- The mesh may have at most 200,000 triangles; the triangles, with identical\n  vertices joined, must form a single closed manifold shell with positive\n  volume, and its volume may change by at most 0.5% when the solid is united\n  with itself.\n\n`movement.json`:\n\n```\n{\n  \"case_centre\": [x, y],\n  \"fixed\": [\"main_plate\", \"bridge\", ...],\n  \"mobiles\": {\n    \"some_name\": {\"axis\": [x, y], \"parts\": [\"wheel_a\", \"arbor_a\", ...]},\n    ...\n  },\n  \"meshes\": [\n    {\"driver\": \"barrel\", \"driver_teeth\": 96, \"driven\": \"some_name\", \"driven_teeth\": 12},\n    ...\n  ],\n  \"hands\": {\n    \"hour\":    {\"mobile\": \"...\", \"part\": \"...\"},\n    \"minute\":  {\"mobile\": \"...\", \"part\": \"...\"},\n    \"seconds\": {\"mobile\": \"...\", \"part\": \"...\"}\n  }\n}\n```\n\n- `fixed`: parts that do not move (plates, bridges, pillars, cocks). Fixed parts\n  must not overlap one another.\n- `mobiles`: each mobile is a set of parts that turn together as one rigid body\n  about the vertical line through `axis`. Parts of one mobile may overlap each\n  other. Do not list `barrel`; it already exists.\n- `meshes`: every pair of gears that drive one another, with the tooth count of\n  the gear on each mobile. All meshes are external (the two mobiles turn in\n  opposite directions). Speeds are worked out from these tooth counts as exact\n  fractions, starting from the barrel.\n- `hands`: which mobile carries each hand, and which of that mobile's parts is\n  the hand.\n- A part may be used only once.\n\n## Hard requirements\n\nIf either fails the score is 0.\n\n- Files: `movement.json` and every part it names are valid as described above.\n- Assembled: in the positions given, the fixed parts taken together and each\n  mobile (the barrel included) intersect one another by at most 0.01 mm3, and no\n  two fixed parts intersect each other by more than 0.01 mm3.\n\n## Scored requirements\n\nEach passes or fails. Weights in brackets; the total is 17.\n\n- **Free to turn [1].** Each mobile, turned through a full turn in 72 steps of 5\n  degrees, never intersects the fixed parts by more than 0.01 mm3.\n- **Held [2].** Each mobile, the barrel included, is moved 0.3 along +x, -x, +y,\n  -y, +z and -z in turn and must intersect what holds it by more than 0.01 mm3\n  every time. For the four sideways moves, anything else counts (fixed parts and\n  other mobiles). For the two moves along z, only the fixed parts and mobiles on\n  the same axis (within 0.01) count: a wheel may not be kept in place by a wheel\n  on a different arbor. So each mobile can turn but cannot wander.\n- **The train runs [3].** No mobile is given two different speeds by the\n  declared meshes, each of the three hand mobiles is driven from the barrel, and\n  every declared mesh passes this test. Starting from the assembled position,\n  at step i (i = 0, 1, ..., 8 x max(driver teeth, driven teeth) - 1) the driver\n  is turned counter-clockwise (seen from +z) by i x 360 / (8 x driver teeth)\n  degrees about its axis and the driven mobile clockwise by that angle x driver\n  teeth / driven teeth about its own. Then\n  - at every step the two mobiles intersect by at most 0.01 mm3 (no jam);\n  - at every fourth step the smallest distance between them is at most 0.1\n    (they stay engaged);\n  - at every eighth step, turning the driver a further quarter of its tooth\n    pitch (90 / driver teeth degrees, counter-clockwise) while the driven mobile\n    is held makes them intersect by more than 0.01 mm3 (the teeth really drive).\n- **Nothing else collides [1].** Every pair of mobiles that does not mesh is\n  turned together at the speeds the tooth counts give (a mobile that is not\n  driven stands still): 144 equal steps covering one full turn of the faster of\n  the two, then 144 equal steps covering one full turn of one relative to the\n  other. At every step they intersect by at most 0.01 mm3.\n- **Hour hand [2], minute hand [2], seconds hand [2], hand arrangement [1].** The\n  watch must tell the time: the hands must move as the hands of a watch do. A\n  hand is driven only through meshes that pass the test of \"The train runs\": a\n  declared mesh that fails that test drives nothing, so the hand speeds are\n  worked out from the barrel through the passing meshes only. (The same holds\n  for the 24-hour hand of stages 2 and 3.)\n- **Hands reach [1].** Each hand part reaches at least 5.0 from its axis.\n- **Size [1].** Everything, as it turns, stays within 20.7 of the vertical line\n  through `case_centre`, and the whole movement including the barrel is at most\n  13.4 tall in z. These limits are the same at every stage.\n- **Printable [1].** The smallest printable feature is 0.2. Each of your parts\n  (not the barrel) is tested like this: it is turned into voxels on a 0.05 grid,\n  a voxel being solid when its centre is inside the part. A solid voxel survives\n  if its centre is at least 0.075 (1.5 voxels) from the centre of the nearest\n  voxel that is not solid. The printable body is every solid voxel whose centre\n  is within 0.05 of a surviving voxel's centre. The part passes if something\n  survives and no solid voxel's centre is further than 0.2 from the printable\n  body. Ordinary gear teeth of module 0.12 or more pass; a wall, web or roof 0.2\n  thick or less does not. How the grid lines up with your part is not fixed, so\n  leave a little margin.\n\n## Score\n\n```\np     = (weight of scored requirements passed) / 17\nscore = 0 if a hard requirement fails, otherwise\nscore = 0.5 * p^2 + 0.5 * (1 if every scored requirement passes, else 0)\n```\n\n## Stage 2: add a 24-hour hand\n\nYou receive a finished stage-1 movement in `work/` (the same files are in\n`previous/` for reference). Add a **24-hour hand**: a fourth hand that shows day\nand night. Declare it as `\"day\"` under `hands`.\n\nWhat is frozen:\n\n- every mobile of the received movement keeps its name and its axis (the same\n  two numbers, unchanged);\n- every part file of those mobiles stays byte-for-byte the same and stays in its\n  mobile (you may add new parts to a mobile);\n- every declared mesh stays, and the hour, minute and seconds entries under\n  `hands` stay.\n\nYou may add mobiles, add parts, add meshes, and replace or add fixed parts.\n\nHard requirements: the two of stage 1, the frozen items above, and a 24-hour\nhand is declared (`hands.day` names a mobile and one of that mobile's parts,\nand that part is a new part, not one of the received parts).\n\nScored requirements (total weight 21): all eleven of stage 1, still passing with\ntheir weights, plus\n\n- **24-hour hand [3].** It moves as a 24-hour hand does.\n- **24-hour hand placement [1].** Its axis is at least 6.0 from the hour hand's\n  axis, and the hand part reaches at least 3.0 from its own axis.\n\nScore: the stage-1 formula with p out of 21.\n\n## Stage 3: change request, a faster barrel\n\nYou receive a finished stage-2 movement in `work/` (the same files are in\n`previous/` for reference). The barrel is replaced by one that is identical in\nevery way (same `meshes/barrel.stl`, same place, same teeth) except that it turns\n**clockwise once every 6 hours** instead of once every 8. Rework the movement so\nthat it meets every requirement of stage 2 with this barrel, and keep as many of\nthe received part files as you can.\n\nNothing is frozen: you may change, add, remove and rename anything. The hard\nrequirements are the two of stage 1, plus: **the change request is met**, that\nis, the hour hand, minute hand, seconds hand and 24-hour hand requirements all\npass with the barrel turning once every 6 hours. The scored requirements are all thirteen of\nstage 2 with their weights (total 21), tested with the barrel turning once every\n6 hours. The hands must still move as the hands of a watch do, and the 24-hour\nhand as a 24-hour hand does.\n\nKept parts. A received part (a part named in the received `movement.json`) is\n**kept** if its file in your submission is byte-for-byte the same as the received\nfile and\n\n- for a received fixed part: it is still listed under `fixed`;\n- for a received part of a mobile: it is still in a mobile of the same name, whose\n  axis is the same as the received mobile's axis (the same two numbers,\n  unchanged), and that mobile is driven from the barrel through declared meshes\n  that pass the test of \"The train runs\".\n\nA received file that is not named in your `movement.json`, that moves to another\nmobile, to a renamed mobile or to `fixed`, or that sits on a mobile nothing drives,\nis not kept.\n\n```\nkept share = (received part files that are kept) / (received part files)\nfactor     = min(1, kept share / (15/17))\np          = (weight of scored requirements passed) / 21\nscore      = 0 if a hard requirement fails, otherwise\nscore      = (0.5 * p^2 + 0.5 * (1 if every scored requirement passes, else 0)) * factor\n```\n\nThe share counts part files: each file counts once, whatever its size or what it\nholds. 15/17 (about 0.882) is the kept share of a reference solution, which keeps 15 of\nthe 17 part files it receives. The factor is exactly 1 at a kept share of 15/17\nor more.\n\n## Stage 4: assemble it\n\nYou receive a finished stage-3 movement in `work/` (also in `previous/`).\n`movement.json` and every part file are frozen: byte-for-byte unchanged.\n\nWrite `work/assembly.json`:\n\n```\n{\"order\": [\"part_name\", ...], \"paths\": {\"part_name\": [P, P, ...], ...}}\n```\n\n`order` lists every part named in `movement.json`, and `barrel`, in the order\nthey are put in. A name that is not a part is ignored; a name that appears more\nthan once counts at its first place only. A part that is not in `order` is not\ninstalled, and it stands in its assembled position from the start, so every part\nin `order` is tested against it. Each P is a 4x4 matrix as four rows of four numbers that moves\nthe part from its assembled position (`world = R * assembled + t`, last row\n`0 0 0 1`); the parts are given in their assembled position, so the last pose of\nevery path is the identity.\n\nRules for a path:\n\n1. Every matrix is finite and a proper rotation plus translation (R^T R = I and\n   det R = +1, within 1e-6); the last pose is the identity within 1e-6.\n2. In the first pose the part's bounding box lies wholly outside the bounding box\n   of the complete movement (all parts and the barrel, assembled) grown by 5.0 on\n   every side.\n3. Between consecutive poses no vertex of the part moves more than 0.2.\n4. At least 2 and at most 1,500 poses.\n5. In every pose the part intersects each part placed before it by at most\n   0.01 mm3. Parts of the same mobile are pressed onto each other and are not\n   tested against one another. The barrel counts as a part of the mobile `barrel`.\n\nA part whose path obeys rules 1 to 5 is installed. A part that breaks a rule is\nnot installed, but it still stands in its assembled position for the parts that\nfollow.\n\n```\np     = (parts installed) / (all parts, the barrel included)\nscore = 0 if the Files requirement of stage 1 fails, if movement.json or a part file was changed,\n        or if assembly.json cannot be read\nscore = 0.5 * p^2 + 0.5 * (1 if every part is installed, else 0)\n```\n\n## What you are given to work with\n\nThere are no measuring tools and no copy of the grader's test code. Every test\nabove is defined completely by its numbers, so you can build your own checks.\n\n- Python 3 with `cadquery` 2.8.0 (OpenCASCADE, importable as `cadquery` and\n  `OCP`), `manifold3d`, `trimesh`, `numpy` and `scipy`.\n- `tools/kernel.py`: small helpers on top of `manifold3d` (read and write STL,\n  used for the supplied barrel and for your own checks; rigid transform, intersection volume, smallest distance, cross-section), plus\n  `write_step(path, shape)` (a CadQuery object or OCP shape, written in\n  millimetres) and `load_step_part(...)`, which turns a STEP file into the same\n  `manifold3d` solid the grader uses. `python3 tools/submit.py` calls it with the\n  numbers stated under \"What you submit\", so a part that submit accepts is the\n  solid the tests see.\n- `meshes/barrel.stl` (the supplied barrel, the only mesh; your parts are STEP).\n- `python3 tools/submit.py`: checks the file format only (JSON structure, part\n  names, each part file read and turned into a solid exactly as described under\n  \"What you submit\") and copies your work to the submission folder: the\n  `movement.json`, the part files it names, `assembly.json` if present, and\n  `scripts/` (at most 200 files and 4,194,304 bytes; larger is a format error).\n  It answers \"accepted\" or a format error. It runs none of the tests.\n\nOnly the submission folder as it is when you stop is graded. You may submit as\noften as you like; the last accepted submission counts.","lineStart":1,"lineEnd":334,"totalLines":334,"truncated":false}},"title":"app/SPEC_WATCH.md","time":{"start":1794645954112,"end":1794645954121}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_1d93c0e3d001LtWHLhwsRq7J7u","sessionID":"ses_e26c3f8acffeWBLPvCcDgQ9v3e","messageID":"msg_1d93c0833001LYa4PN0dNHc0zh"}}

ASCII\n        try:\n            text = data.decode(\"ascii\")\n        except UnicodeDecodeError:\n            raise FormatError(\"neither a binary STL of the declared length nor ASCII\")\n        vals = []\n        for line in text.splitlines():\n            p = line.split()\n            if len(p) == 4 and p[0] == \"vertex\":\n                try:\n                    vals.append((float(p[1]), float(p[2]), float(p[3])))\n                except ValueError:\n                    raise FormatError(\"non-numeric vertex coordinate\")\n                if len(vals) > 3 * max_triangles:\n                    raise FormatError(\"more than %d triangles\" % max_triangles)\n        if not vals or len(vals) % 3:\n            raise FormatError(\"no complete triangles found\")\n        tris = np.array(vals, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, 3, 3)\n    if len(tris) == 0:\n        raise FormatError(\"no triangles\")\n    if not np.isfinite(tris).all():\n        raise FormatError(\"non-finite vertex coordinate\")\n    return tris\n\n\ndef write_stl(path, man):\n    mesh = man.to_mesh()\n    v = np.asarray(mesh.vert_properties, dtype=np.float32)[:, :3]\n    t = np.asarray(mesh.tri_verts)\n    tris = v[t]\n    nrm = np.cross(tris[:, 1] - tris[:, 0], tris[:, 2] - tris[:, 0])\n    ln = np.linalg.norm(nrm, axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    nrm = np.where(ln > 0, nrm / np.where(ln > 0, ln, 1), 0)\n    rec = np.zeros(len(tris), dtype=np.dtype([(\"n\", \"<f4\", 3), (\"v\", \"<f4\", (3, 3)), (\"a\", \"<u2\")]))\n    rec[\"n\"], rec[\"v\"] = nrm, tris\n    with open(path, \"wb\") as f:\n        f.write(b\"board-in-a-box\".ljust(80, b\" \"))\n        f.write(struct.pack(\"<I\", len(tris)))\n        f.write(rec.tobytes())\n\n\ndef raw_volume(tris):\n    return float(np.einsum(\"ij,ij->i\", tris[:, 0], np.cross(tris[:, 1], tris[:, 2])).sum() / 6.0)\n\n\ndef tris_to_manifold(tris):\n    \"\"\"Weld identical vertices and build a Manifold. 3).astype(np.uint32)\n    keep = (faces[:, 0] != faces[:, 1]) & (faces[:, 1] != faces[:, 2]) & (faces[:, 0] != faces[:, 2])\n    faces = faces[keep]\n    man = m3.Manifold(m3.Mesh(vert_properties=verts, tri_verts=faces))\n    if man.status() != m3.Error.NoError:\n        raise FormatError(\"mesh is not a closed manifold (%s)\" % man.status().name)\n deflection (radians),\n# and the triangles then go through the same path as an STL (tris_to_part).\ndef read_step(path, max_bytes, max_triangles, linear_deflection, angular_deflection,\n              max_triangle_faces, timeout_s, memory_mb):\n    \"\"\"Triangles (N x 3 x 3, mm) of the one solid in a STEP file, or FormatError.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n    try:\n        size = os.path.getsize(path)\n    except OSError:\n        raise FormatError(\"cannot be read\")\n    if size > max_bytes:\n        raise FormatError(\"file larger than %d bytes\" % max_bytes)\n    with open(path, \"rb\") as f:\n        head = f.read(64).lstrip()\n    if not head.startswith(b\"ISO-10303-21;\"):\n        raise FormatError(\"not a STEP file (must start with ISO-10303-21;)\")\n    cmd =
